newsitem.title: GERMANY: Low Rhine water levels add to feed transport costs.
newsitem.headline: Low Rhine water levels add to feed transport costs.

text.p: Rain will be needed in the next few weeks to boost low water levels on the Rhine and its tributaries, which have added to feeds shipping costs, a source at the German feeds industry association said.
"It is not yet a market factor as automatic surcharges are often triggered by low levels," he said.
"But rain would help prevent further falls in the water levels before melting snow in the Alps fills up rivers in the winter months," he said.
Levels today in Kaub were 107 centimetres above zero and 158 cm in Cologne, compared with 131 cm in Kaub and 186 cm in Cologne a month ago, according to Dutch state water authority figures.
Soymeal from seed crushers in Mainz and Mannheim carried a 0.75 marks surcharge per 100 kg while surcharges on rapemeal and soymeal further north were around 0.40-0.60 marks, traders said.
Compound feed producers still needed to buy some raw materials for the autumn and winter months and prices were already underpinned by firm dollar levels versus the mark, they added.
